summary: Intermittent 5xxs for enterprise customer during high-priority queue starvation
description:
Issue summary: BrightHealth Analytics reports intermittent 5xx responses starting 2026-03-10 14:10 UTC. Errors are concentrated on high-priority inference routes and coincide with bursts of long-sequence embedding + generate hybrid requests. Impact: customer is seeing ~12% of requests fail with 5xx (mostly 502/504) and some sessions drop mid-stream. Business impact: degraded feature availability for customer-facing analytics dashboards during business hours.

Observed behavior: API gateway returns 502/504 for affected requests. Upstream logs show serving-runtime container restart loops on several nodes attributed to native runtime worker crashes when serving long-sequence requests under high concurrency. Autoscaler activity shows rapid scale-ups then thrashing as nodes fail health checks. Circuit breakers in gateway flip briefly and reset.

Environment: Production; customers' requests routed to high-priority queue (customer configured) in us-east-1, traffic spike started ~2026-03-10 14:05 UTC and persisted intermittently for ~2 hours.

Why this is plausible: workload pattern has heavy synchronous generate calls with sequence lengths >2048 tokens which increases KV caching pressure; combined with aggressive preemption/placement from autoscaler, certain GPU instances are experiencing kernel-level OOMs and process-level crashes which bubble up as 502/504 at API gateway.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Have an enterprise account with a high-priority queue configured.
2) Send mixed request stream: 30% long-sequence generate requests (seq_len ~2300 tokens) and 70% embedding requests concurrently at ~1200 rps for 5 minutes.
3) Observe increase in 5xx rates from API gateway and repeated serving-runtime container restarts on a subset of nodes.
4) Reproduce window is intermittent and requires sustained concurrency to trigger accelerator memory pressure.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC - SRE (Marco): initial triage shows node-level OOMs correlated with requests that have seq_len >2000; kernel logs show 'CUDA out of memory' on multiple pods.

2026-03-10 15:05 UTC - Support (Aisha): customer confirms they rolled out an internal batch job at 14:00 which increased concurrent embedding requests; they paused the job and error rate dropped but then resurged when regular traffic increased.

2026-03-10 15:30 UTC - Eng (Lina): identified scheduler race where preemption of lower-priority pods for burst capacity incorrectly evicts warm inference workers, causing cold restarts and increased memory pressure on remaining pods.

2026-03-11 09:10 UTC - Dev (Marco): reproduced in staging with a synthetic workload; crash occurs after ~200 concurrent long-seq requests due to KV cache thrashing and unbounded per-request memory accounting bug (see PR #522).
comments: Aisha Patel (2026-03-10 14:25 UTC): Logged by customer via support portal. Captured stack traces and link to request ids in logs above.
BrightHealth Ops (2026-03-10 14:40 UTC): We temporarily throttled outgoing jobs; errors reduced but not eliminated. Please advise if we should route to a different priority queue.
Marco Liu (SRE) (2026-03-10 15:10 UTC): We're investigating kernel OOMs and will test a conservative autoscaler policy to avoid aggressive preemption. Assigning INT-876 to track scheduler fix.
Lina Gomez (Infra) (2026-03-11 09:20 UTC): PR #522 contains a patch that bounds per-request GPU memory reservation and avoids KV cache thrash; testing in staging now.
Aisha Patel (2026-03-11 11:05 UTC): Customer accepted temporary mitigation: reduced high-priority weight and enabled fallback to a lower-memory model variant. Monitoring for 24 hours.
resolution: Mitigation applied (2026-03-11): temporarily reduced high-priority queue weight for BrightHealth, enabled automatic fallback to a lower-memory model variant for requests with seq_len >1800, and applied conservative autoscaler policy to avoid preemption-induced thrashing. Engineering patch (PR #522) to bound per-request GPU reservations is scheduled for rollout to prod on 2026-03-13. Follow-ups: validate autoscaler behavior under mixed priority workloads and add guarded KV cache eviction to prevent future thrash.
next_steps: Roll out PR #522 to production with canary on subset of us-east cluster (owner: Lina Gomez)
Add a synthetic regression test that simulates mixed long-seq generate + embedding workload (owner: Marco Liu)
Update runbook to include knob to temporarily lower priority weights for enterprise customers during large internal batch jobs (owner: Support)
